items.title: Headline scores
items.caption: YOLO26x scores 0.870 / 0.698 and RF-DETR Large 0.876 / 0.679 (mAP@50 / mAP@50:95); the two used different validation sets, so this is not a head-to-head ranking.

items.title: Frames per route
items.caption: 23,551 frames from five routes plus a ZED stereo-camera set, split by train and validation.

items.title: Boxes per class
items.caption: Labelled boxes per class across train (solid) and validation (faded): 38,386 masts, 38,189 contact points, 31,272 pantographs and 25,398 arms.

items.title: Webcam and ZED
items.caption: Most frames come from a standard webcam; 1,310 come from a ZED stereo camera that was being considered as its replacement.

items.title: Boxes per frame
items.caption: Most frames hold two to six boxes; 2,297 frames carry no annotation at all, and every one of 30 sampled shows a pantograph, so they are unlabelled frames rather than true negatives.

items.title: Box sizes by class
items.caption: Contact-point boxes are tiny (about 2% of the frame width) while pantographs are large; a few pixels of offset costs a contact point most of its overlap score.

items.title: Where boxes sit in the frame
items.caption: Pantographs sit low and central, contact points hug the top edge of the pantograph, masts line the edges and arms cluster below it: a strong spatial prior for the detector.

items.title: The logged route
items.caption: The logged GPS run between Gonda and Bahraich: 1,188 fixes covering about 71 km.

items.title: The labelling pipeline
items.caption: Film, pre-annotate with a small detector, track between keyframes, review every frame in CVAT, then export and train.

items.title: How the data was split
items.caption: Splits keep whole video segments together (no segment appears in both train and validation); the mast-focused set was added at training time and RF-DETR's valid and test were cut from the YOLO validation set by image.

items.title: Project timeline
items.caption: Proof of concept in Nov 2025, depth exploration through the winter, the labelling campaign in May-June 2026, then YOLO26x (10-23 Jun) and RF-DETR (29-30 Jun) training.

items.title: Where the shapes came from
items.caption: CVAT records how each of 119,972 shapes entered the tool: mostly imported labels that were reviewed, plus tracked, model-assisted, semi-automatic and hand-drawn shapes.

items.title: YOLO26x training curve
items.caption: Validation mAP over all 200 epochs; the best mAP@50:95 (0.6976) came at epoch 178, and the final epochs sit at about 0.694.

items.title: RF-DETR training curve
items.caption: Validation mAP over 35 epochs; the best mAP@50:95 (0.6786) came at epoch 34 of 35, with improvement slowing towards the end.

items.title: Training and validation losses
items.caption: Both detectors converge smoothly; the validation loss flattens well before the end, which is why more epochs bought very little.

items.title: Per-class AP
items.caption: Pantograph is strong for both models (0.90-0.92) while contact_point sits near 0.39 for both: a data and box-size limit more than a model one.

items.title: Where the label gaps are
items.caption: 1,266 frames show a contact point without a pantograph box: about 14% of Mumbai, 8% of Mehsana and Palanpur, and 3% of Ahmedabad and Lucknow. The list is kept for review.
